headline: Biomedical predictors move toward cross-cohort testing and standardized benchmarks
label: Cross Cohort Biomedical Prediction Evaluation
summary: PRTS and TabBioMed test prediction across cohorts and curated datasets, while TISCH3, DriverDBv5 and PDAC BioPortal expand reference data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is that evaluation design limits what a biomedical predictive claim can support. PRTS, a 220M-parameter in-context learning model, predicts clinical endpoints from bulk transcriptomes across diseases and platforms without per-cohort training. TabBioMed standardizes preprocessing across 94 curated public tabular datasets and compares 23 models. Foundation models lead, but tree-based methods remain relevant baselines. Elflow pairs automated QC with VICReg self-supervised representations and is benchmarked on public flow and CyTOF datasets. HIT-Fuse addresses missing modalities when fusing six omics and pathomics inputs. SpaceMACE adds spatial context to tumour-cell annotation. A parallel strand expands the reference data these evaluations depend on. TISCH3 grows to 477 tumour-microenvironment datasets, including 69 spatial collections. DriverDBv5 examines whether multi-omics drivers carry prognostic weight. PDAC BioPortal integrates bulk, single-nucleus and spatial pancreatic cancer cohorts. What is new is the emphasis on cross-platform transfer and standardized comparison. These items do not establish whether curated public benchmarks reflect performance under deployment conditions.
